newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan-China trade up 7.2 pct yr/yr in Jan-March.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan-China trade up 7.2 pct yr/yr in Jan-March.

text.p: Taiwan's trade with rival China grew 7.2 percent to US$5.187 billion in the first three months of 1997 compared to the same 1996 period, the cabinet's Board of Foreign Trade said on Tuesday.
Taiwan's exports to the communist mainland rose an annual five percent in January-March to $4.337 billion, while imports rose 20.1 percent to $850 million, a board statement said.

The board attributed the stable export growth to China's improved exports in the first quarter, increasing its demand for Taiwanese materials. Due to a recovering economy in Taiwan, the island's industrial output and exports grew steadily, fuelling demand for China's agricultural and industrial materials, especially in the information and telecommunications industries, the statement said.
In January-March, Taiwan enjoyed a trade surplus of $3.488 billion, up 1.9 percent year-on-year, it said.

In March alone, two-way trade surged 24.2 percent to $2.013 billion from a year earlier, with exports to China up 20.2 percent to $1.721 billion and imports up 54.6 percent to $291 million, it said. The board said the global recovery had helped boost exports from both Taiwan and China, in turn triggering higher trade growth between the rival economies.

China has considered Taiwan a renegade province since a civil war separated them in 1949. Taiwan bans direct contact with China. All trade with China must be conducted through a third region, mostly Hong Kong.
Some 30,000 Taiwan firms have invested more than $30 billion in China since an unofficial thaw began in the late 1980s. Trade has grown despite a new political freeze dating to mid-1995.
